title: Dynamic self-learning local reviewer: keryx ships the mechanism, the project owns the people

AC1.note: src/gdskills/bundled-no-persona.test.ts enumerates the bundled tree and fails on the persona word or a home-directory path. It caught a surviving --boss flag in CI that a skill-name search missed.

AC2.note: Skill and rule rewritten from scratch describing the mechanism; renamed to code-learned-review rather than keeping a persona name for a de-personalised mechanism.

AC3.note: .metaproject/review-learning.config.json names skill, repo and authors; lives in the project, never in bundled. Absent config returns null and prints one plain line, exit 0.

AC4.note: keryx review learn --pr <n> reads the durable pr-comments record and calls the existing learnProjectSkill. No re-fetch, no second learning path.

AC5.note: Two-author test with one configured; the unconfigured author's text appears in no proposal. Disabling the filter turns 5 tests red.

AC6.note: learn still writes only a proposal; apply remains the only writer. This flow added a producer, not a second applier.

AC7.note: learn.ts already refused targets outside .metaproject/project-skills. The new tests pin that behaviour with src/gdskills/bundled as the named target; removing the check turns 2 red.

AC8.note: cli-reference.md documents seeding from conventions the operator already holds, stating plainly the source is their own copy outside this repository and that keryx keeps nothing.

AC9.note: End-to-end test runs collect-from-fixtures -> filter -> propose -> apply and asserts the lesson in the local SKILL.md with the version bumped.

AC10.note: No enforcement claim was made without a wire. The record lacked comment bodies, so rather than claim a join that could not work, SeenComment gained a bounded body and older records report as bodyless.

AC11.note: Both trees carry every edit; 171 mirrored files compared byte-for-byte with 0 diffs; mirror and build-parity guards pass.

AC12.note: typecheck clean; bun test 6113 pass / 18 skip; test:guards 161/0; check:doc-links 1131 links / 0 broken. The single failure is the known nondeterministic SAC test, present in the baseline.
